chunks: With this chain of transmission, from 'Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Malik ibn A'yan, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about one who performed wudu (ablution) and forgot al-madmadah and al-istinshaq, then remembered after he had entered into his salat (prayer). He said: “There is no harm.”

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْشَاقَ: drawing water into the nose during wudu (ablution)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; no legal problem

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets al-madmadah and al-istinshaq in wudu (ablution) and remembers after starting salat (prayer), is the prayer still valid?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer). It indicates that if someone forgets rinsing the mouth and inhaling water into the nose during wudu (ablution), then remembers only after beginning salat (prayer), there is no problem, showing these acts are not obligatory elements whose omission invalidates the prayer.
